00659d49-eb82-54cf-9b2e-b22c11ab0717.description: The Peace Treaty of Drinápoly (Adrianapolis). Bálint Bakfark (Valentin Greff Bakfark) whose lute pieces were published in Lyon (1552) lives at the Transylvanian princely court (in 1572 moves to Padua).

0128476d-7312-5ce8-ac24-2c23c977cf39.description: The Italian Communist Party is formed.

01d2538a-239b-581a-b251-55aa27fdbcf9.description: Friedrich I Barbarossa (1152–90) of the Hohenstaufen Dynasty is crowned emperor. He drowned during the Third Crusade near Konya in Turkey in 1190.

02880ab8-3d74-563e-ac9f-29597c97885e.description: Battle at Krbavsko Polje after which Ottoman armies overran most of Croatia and Islamisation followed, particularly in the so-called ‘Turkish Croatia’ between the Una and Vrbas rivers.

0386d824-b32a-5c48-ab12-082ca4cc996b.description: Death of Luís de Camões. Loss of independence: Phillip II of Spain becomes king of Portugal as Phillip I.

0425d2fe-8d40-582f-b746-ae97561065e4.description:
Petar Zrinski and Fran Krsto Frankopan executed in Wiener Neustadt (Bečko Novo Mjesto).  
Building of Dubrovnik Cathedral after the plan of A. Buffalini from Urbino which displays features of developed Roman Baroque.

045abd99-94ac-5442-86c8-b909eface676.description: Origination of the Moravian Margraviate as part of the Czech state, with main centres Znojmo, Brno and Olomouc.

04c52375-54dd-5b87-bc2a-e72106af3078.description: Anti-Habsburg revolution and freedom fight (from March 15) led by Lajos Kossuth. Independent Hungarian government (Prime Minister: Count Lajos Batthyány). Hungarian victory in the battle of Pákozd.

05240e2c-4d19-5f15-8e04-8c045fd0d020.description: The Battle of Nándorfehérvár (Belgrade): János Hunyadi defeats the attacking Turks led by Sultan Mehmed II. After his victory Hunyadi dies from plague in the military camp.

05254a3f-4377-5e76-a0c6-35a2e616a9ae.description: Turks occupy a large part of north Croatia.

069bafaa-d920-567f-9912-88a101c4031e.description: Zadar rebels against Venice and allies with Hungary.

06b6c807-8eae-5482-8c38-084b5a56700a.description: Issue of the Charter of Felicianus mentioning the founder of the Diocese, King Ladislas, the first bishop of Zagreb, Bishop Duh, and other clergy.

08c4c5ff-df50-524c-94f3-abfa594fdc41.description: Jesuits build their church in Rijeka. Dedicated to St Vitus it is the first and the biggest circular Baroque building in Croatia.

08d61b77-ee9b-5c38-ba30-eb1cdb7ddf07.description: Turks occupy several Hungarian fortresses in the new Turkish wars. At the siege of Eger fewer than 2,000 Hungarians led by István Dobó triumph over the attacking 60–70,000 Turks.

092662d1-2347-546a-9632-05bea2c604ae.description: The establishment of Great Moravia (Moravia, western Slovakia, parts of Hungary, Austria, Bohemia and Poland).

095b1256-7d77-5543-bacd-4e3ecd151770.description: The Council of Trent begins, to end in 1563. The Council marks the beginning of the Counter-Reformation.

097e3f00-ddd9-5f10-9475-99e80e57d36d.description: Abbasid revolt in Beja, which quickly spreads to all of al-Gharb.

0a4a8c15-7630-5f2e-899d-e55e7daaf2fd.description: Birth of Leonardo da Vinci, artist, scientist and inventor who will enrich Italian culture with works of great renown, such as the Mona Lisa and Lady with an Ermine.

0aa6d34c-b52d-5143-8be7-94168c0abdea.description: Defeat of the Klis, the last southern fortress. Ottomans constitute the Sanđak of Klis.

0b9ee5c7-4f89-5113-9eeb-a0e5f22fb16c.description: Friedrich II (1215–50), Emperor of the Hohenstaufen Dynasty and King of Sicily, becomes King of Jerusalem during the Fifth Crusade. He was influenced by Islamic traditions.

0c94bd94-0dd8-5f33-90ab-b78950e16678.description: The Croatian People’s Peasants’ Party – from 7 December Republican Peasants’ Party – led by Stjepan Radić refuses to acknowledge the monarchy and leads Croats to ethnic and political emancipation.

0cb0ac39-cf07-5cc9-af5b-e8951cb1cd5c.description: After writing the Summa de paenintentia Paulus Hungarus, a canon lawyer, returns from Bologna and organises the Dominican order in Hungary. French architect Villard de Honnecourt visits Hungary.

0cee69c0-c2ab-5846-bd78-80fd2dfa11d3.description: Austria-Hungary reincorporates the military border into Croatia, increasing the number of ethnic Serbs in Croatia to about 25 per cent.

0d20a737-fdaa-5d16-befc-57163109c27e.description: Crowning of the first Croatian king, Stjepan Držislav (969–97), a member of the Trpimirović Dynasty. The Byzantine Emperor Basil II gave him symbols of royal power.

0dd269e8-1206-539a-9eaa-6c48b48d34a2.description: Establishment of the Czech Engineering School in Prague. New patent against non-Catholics. Heresy declared a crime against the state, non-Catholics punishable by death.

0e482f06-3139-5db4-b9b0-4c112e8f8c9c.description: Founding of Olomouc bishopric. Vratislav II made first Czech King (1085). The first Czech chronicle known as the *Chronicle of Cosmas*. Premonstratensian and Cistercian monasteries founded (1140).

0e7ef834-ca6c-55e0-a5eb-e6df1c1fd695.description: In Dubrovnik the Jesuit church of St Ignatius is built according to the plans of Andrea Pozzo.

0f5c0f8a-1df6-5ff3-9e8f-486a84ce695c.description: Peace in Srijemski Karlovci. The end of Turkish rule in north Croatia It remained under the rule of Habsburgs while south Croatia, with the exception of Dubrovnik Republic, was dominated by Venice.

119ae54f-6af5-58e2-a8d4-73849fda4173.description: The Arab conquest of Sicily is complete with the fall of Rometta, the last Byzantine stronghold.

1206f958-8d26-599b-8ab7-af03b18c92a3.description: Austria takes Milan and the Kingdom of Naples.

12206946-0e55-501d-9903-1dc58d41b387.description: King Otto III (983–1002) is crowned emperor in Rome by Pope Gregory V (996–9).

1275c936-7ad2-5a66-ab12-52a02e65089a.description: Jesuit mathematician Ruđer Bošković publishes his work *De natura et usu infinitorum et infinite parvorum* in Rome.

13d623f5-5fb3-5a18-8bf6-412d7dba1fd9.description: Pico della Mirandola (1463–94) writes Oration on the Dignity of Man, an expression of the new Renaissance humanist culture that exalted man’s dignity and right to self-determination.

15235ae7-96dc-5dde-a931-4569bc5e2ca8.description: Expulsion of the Jews and the Muslims.

155cf875-e84b-5a52-a051-2969e1423c60.description: Work starts on the Hieronymites Monastery.

1588b62b-4118-5024-985d-cdc408270890.description: First war of independence: Charles Albert of Savoy, King of Sardinia (1831–49) leads a coalition of Italian states to drive the Austrians from the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia.

161b4e1a-5462-52cd-bd36-7b259be4009d.description: Establishment of towns. German colonisation. Invasion of the Mongolians (1241). Introduction of mining law (1249), the provincial court (1253) and provincial statutes. The Inquisition introduced (1257).

16c184f3-1d28-5f00-85bf-196db37b594a.description: Roger II, governor of Sicily since 1112, is crowned King of Sicily and reigns until 1154.

19df9fe5-7be7-5868-8a89-c63cf0bf3e65.description: A notary of King Béla III (Anonymus ‘Magister P.’) writes a chronicle of the Hungarian conquest and settlement (Gesta Hungarorum). The beginning of the rebuilding of the Kalocsa abbey (built in the 11th century).

19fc9919-0bf7-53c6-a3c6-3fcc3c5524eb.description: The authority of the Hungarian-Croatian parliament over Croatian internal legal questions is acknowledged at the joint council at Požun.

1a13e752-be00-570b-80af-f555b2aa1b0f.description: Italy joins the Triple Alliance with Germany and Austria: Italian colonial policy begins.

1b523e4d-466b-5e65-b159-f3b7a97f8678.description: Diet of Pozsony (Pressburg, today: Bratislava, Slovakia): coronation of Maria Theresia (Theresa), daughter of Karl (Charles) VI, as Queen of Hungary. The diet offers military help for the Habsburgs in the Austrian Succession Wars.

1b6d63ea-bd6a-5862-8bfd-056c0c23e0f5.description: Marco Polo, son of a Venetian merchant, departs for China with his father Nicolò and uncle Matteo. He is one of the first Westerners to reach China.

1ba3b7d8-1487-5368-ab84-40b59bd0bd69.description: Jesuit Stjepa Glavač, a professor of the Zagreb Academy, publishes the first domestic geographic map of Croatia, which meets the high standards of cartography of that time in Europe.

1bc6a1c1-dce2-5018-b7c0-4c5bcf71c759.description: Emperor Franz Joseph enters the Dual Monarchy with Hungary. Conflicting interests prevent Austria-Hungary from uniting the South Slavs: Croatia and Slavonia fall under Hungarian control, while Austria retains Dalmatia.

1ca1f9a7-32f3-58cf-8f78-4af4038b392a.description: Joseph II abolishes all male and female religious orders except those which take care of the sick and helpless or are engaged in education.

1e006bc2-aef2-5e16-994f-14de8bfbe5bc.description: The Siege of Vienna by the Ottomans ends in the defeat of the Ottomans by a united army. A gradual retreat of the Ottomans begins.

1e86ed86-6e57-5852-a395-6fd8204091bf.description: The Hanseatic League, an alliance of trading guilds from the cities of Lübeck, Hamburg, Wismar and Rostock is officially founded.

1e968810-7404-5322-95b6-90313ba14106.description: The beginning of the compilation of the Pray codex (contains the first continuous Hungarian texts) and the oldest Hungarian chronicle, the Annals of Pozsony (Pressburg, today: Bratislava, Slovakia).

1ef57012-52d6-59f3-98b4-780e85f343b4.description: Voyage of Bartolomeu Dias around the south of Africa to the Indian Ocean. On his return, he discovers Cape of Storms, renamed the Cape of Good Hope by John II.

1f31a339-f52d-516d-b90d-e0773ec6864e.description: The *Law of Vinodol* is composed, one of the first juridical regulations in this part of Europe.

20094a39-3ce5-5253-a810-3c21e150dbc1.description: Italy’s first parliament is inaugurated in Turin. Victor Emanuel II, King of Sardinia (1849–61), becomes the first king of Italy (1861–78).

21a3ff1d-8fc1-5eb1-9c62-956fe69fdb7f.description: The Buda printing house of András Hess publishes his *Chronica Hungarorum*, a chronicle of Hungary. Fruitless negotiations with Emperor Friedrich III lead Mátyás I to occupy Vienna in 1485.

226bbf08-55b6-5c5f-92e9-3f310a17a92d.description: Emperor Franz Joseph I declares the February Patent and dismisses the Hungarian Diet. Ányos Jedlik invents the dynamo. Compulsory preventive injection against pox introduced in Szabolcs County by Dr Frigyes Korányi.

23716a7d-8df9-51a3-a1f1-8a26a4e7991c.description: Abbasid campaigns in the south. Conquest of Lisbon and Mértola.

23c52810-5645-56fa-83bb-25ed01b105fb.description: Execution of the leaders of the Wesselényi revolt against the Habsburgs. All needs of the Austrian armies based in Hungary paid for by Hungary causing paupery. Continuing oppression of Protestants.

240e40cc-ffe7-5f61-b97f-5749b3fedb69.description: Treaty of Alcanises, which fixes the Portuguese border.

26e54742-58b2-57d5-85c0-421ae7db2f22.description: Mazagán (al-Jadida), the last Portuguese town in Morocco, is abandoned.

27da1ed5-83eb-5b67-b053-cd32827a920f.description: Battle of Muhi: Mongolian troops led by Khan Batu defeat the army of King Béla IV. At the end of the Mongol invasion in 1242 Austrian and Styrian forces also attacked Hungary, which was rebuilt by King Béla IV.

283ccb7e-86c1-5cb4-a636-bdc183f248b0.description: Trianon Peace Treaty: Hungary loses two-thirds of its territory – 190,000 square km – (Transylvania, the Uplands, part of Western, Eastern and Southern Hungary).

2a605298-62aa-5527-a4d2-833f4e9b24bd.description: Consolidation of Almoravid power in the southwest of the peninsula. Attack on Coimbra.

2b24e8f1-46e6-5c02-ac03-6ca9ebe44e9e.description: The first diplomatic agreement of the Croats with the Holy See. They made an agreement with Pope Agaton by which they agreed not to start wars against neighbouring Christian states.

2c494d33-257c-5be9-b11f-1cf1289b2190.description: Founding of the Ottoman governing unit in Middle Slavonia with the centre in Požega. For more than 40 years the governor was Hadži Mehmed-aga who supported Sulayman during the siege of Siget.

2cf5d128-dbbb-5d70-ba8f-24d19a306ba0.description: Movement of nations – invasions of nomadic tribes, arrival of western Slavs from the Danube and Vistula basins. Agrarian-pastoral culture, cremation burials. The empire of Samo – the first tribal union of the Slavs.

2dee7e47-c42c-5c7a-9bde-db4468c567a2.description: Battle of Austerlitz (Battle of Three Emperors). Austria, Prussia and Russia defeated by Napoleon.

2e3dc824-b219-5d24-b852-0975c4b9027a.description: Gregory the Great (590–604) becomes pope. During his pontificate, the Church becomes more independent from the Byzantine Empire and great efforts are made to evangelise the Anglo-Saxons and Lombards.

2e50e46b-3129-56c1-b388-dc243bc08b44.description: Hildegard von Bingen (1098–1179), a mystic and a composer of hymns who had visions of God, collects her visions in the book Scivias (‘Know the Way’).

2e7bc2eb-20c1-510b-9cb1-766ad69dafc0.description: Coronation of King (St) László I who reforms Hungary’s legal codes, administrative and ecclesiastical system and life (1083: canonisation of King István and Prince Imre; 1092: synod of Szabolcs).

2f8c0de7-18c3-5380-ac50-10e2368711d9.description: Ragusa falls into the hands of Lajos (Louis) I (the Great). During Medieval times Hungary was its most extensive under his rule. Compilation of a Hungarian chronicle, the Képes Krónika (Illustrated Chronicle).

3056a5d6-9f4e-5199-94ce-c69a8e0e31fa.description: The Lombards enter Italy. The lands occupied in the Centre and the South become the Duchies of Spoleto and Benevento respectively.

319bb388-676d-570b-93d1-d2ad32b490ba.description: Michelangelo finishes the fresco Last Judgement in the Sistine Chapel.

31ad70ec-9661-5aff-8f82-4541edbb5796.description: On 2 February King Otto I (r. 936–73) of the Ottonian Dynasty, later called Otto the Great, is crowned emperor in Rome.

33c56994-70d0-561e-8afb-b807610c9bf0.description: Basilica of Euphrasius built in Piorec, one of the most important monuments in Croatia. It was built on the remains of an earlier three-naved basilica.

3603f521-2580-58a3-93e3-26410b66a872.description: During the rule of the Merovingian Dynasty (558–629), rulers of the Frankish Dynasty gradually gain power over parts of what will later become Germany.

36c2af70-d678-5173-9943-1477950f4160.description: In the Treaty of Verdun the Frankish Empire is divided into three separate parts called West-, Middle- and East Francia. The Germanic Empire is called the Holy Roman Empire of the German Nation.

3708013d-a9b0-5a72-b18b-a52d7cc0bedf.description: The Church of St Donat in Zadar, first dedicated to Holy Trinity, is built in the 9th century, a great example of Byzantine architecture and the largest circular church of the Carolingian era in Europe.

3725a29f-3ac0-50c8-8e54-30ca96928584.description: Prince Géza is succeeded by his son István who continues the Hungarian conversion to Christianity. Following nomadic tradition Prince Koppány claims the rulership but is defeated and killed.

37953aa2-c725-5fda-9548-109687b477db.description: Dubrovnik recognises the authority of Venice, which will last until 1358. In that period Dubrovnik was obliged to pay Venice annual tribute and to accept Venetians as its dukes and archbishops.

390ed287-b875-52e1-9e1e-ce5fb5fb70e0.description: The Pragmatic Sanction: Charles VI declared the heritability of the Habsburg crown in the female line in default of a male heir, and the indivisibility of the countries of the House of Habsburg. Plague endemics.

395ffdfc-f6e9-5e9f-a52f-86628b1a0370.description: Duke Branimir becomes Banus of Croatia and breaks up with Constantinople. Pope John VIII gave his blessing to the duke and the whole Croatian people, as he informed Branimir in his letters.

3965acc2-2ff9-538e-be4d-7ceab89ccedf.description: The physician Robert Koch (1843–1910) finds the bacillus of the Cholera disease. This is only one of the numerous findings of the pioneer of bacteriology.

3bf148cc-750c-5c81-a5c7-2c45612a27a1.description: Establishment of the first public museums (Opava). The first long-distance railway in Europe (České Budějovice–Linz, 1825). J. E. Purkyně introduces cell theory. Disturbances among workers and peasants.

3c954ce1-9b1e-5d1a-a4ec-19dcea60f22b.description: King Ferdinand I promulgates the Sesmaria law on agriculture.

3d0812b7-c0bc-59d4-b369-6acee42ea0d6.description: The Peace of Augsburg results in recognition of Lutherism and Roman Catholicism. Each ruler now has the right to decide on the religion to be practised in his state.

3d861a60-fc93-5813-9037-33f764d1b6fa.description: Foundation letter of the Benedictine abbey in Tihany by King András I (its Latin text contains the first Hungarian text fragment). András was buried in the abbey church in 1060.

4079685d-befa-5ee7-8291-3060daa23705.description: Travelling artists perform the first opera in Zagreb *I Filosofi imaginari* composed by Giovanni Paisiello, which marks the beginning of the new repertoire including Rossini, Bellini, etc.

4097b3cf-a08c-520e-8f96-662bc7e770f3.description: King Mátyás I dies and the all’ antica Renaissance presence in Hungary (see the Renaissance Buda castle, Mátyás I’s famous Corvina library) wanes. Struggle for the Hungarian throne.

416fd18e-c5ec-5703-b848-247ecc672f74.description: Nikola Zrinski defeats the Pasha of Budim near Bobocsa. The fall of Kostajnica and the arrival of Ottomans in Turopolje.

41f2f19f-7cb0-57d6-b3cf-d74af3f04c52.description: Austro-Hungarian monarchy ends. Charles IV agrees to the form of state chosen by the Hungarian nation but does not abdicate. Count Mihály Károlyi is Prime Minister of the People’s Republic of Hungary, which lays down arms and starts armistice talks.

42264fe0-a6a5-5dd8-8375-12283578bc23.description: The Venetians install Krešimir III (1000–30) as king of Croatia; he ruled with his brother Gojislav. They attempted to restore rule over the Dalmatian cities that were under Venetian control.

4361927e-f8dd-5f9c-b11c-9595d428fd1f.description: On the initiative of Charles VI the Karolina road from Karlovac to Bosilje, Vrbovsko, Mrkopalj, Bakar and Rijeka is built.

4434d2c3-3b87-54be-9dfa-ac22a48dbeea.description: Arrival of the Jesuit order; suppression of non-Catholics. The first independent map of Moravia (1569); the establishment of a university in Olomouc (1573). Fraternal Union published the Kralice Bible (1579); its language became the official norm.

44df37f7-cb4f-59fe-b91e-2769610704e5.description: During the lifetime of Saint Boniface, an English missionary who lived from c. 675 to 754, the tribes in Germany become Christians.

44eff533-c7df-5b44-af8e-f8ff53a17492.description:
The ‘Josephina’ road between Karlovac and Rijeka is constructed.  
The first stockmarket in Rijeka is established.

45023d22-8eb8-525c-8de6-c40ee7d7ade4.description: Pope Kliment XIV issues a bull abolishing the Jesuit order. Establishment of learned societies; compulsory school attendance introduced (1774). Peasant uprisings. Origins of the Czech National Enlightenment. The first history of Moravian art published.

455101e8-27af-57ad-9722-0cde081d853c.description: Reorganisation of the Suebian Church by Saint Martin of Dumes.

45749c10-5f5b-5d95-b13c-83d35835c2a4.description: The wedding of King Lajos II and Mary Habsburg (Mary leaves Hungary after the deaths of Lajos II and as Mary of Hungary later becomes the governor of the Low Countries).

45e97475-9993-5a04-b843-0ef225eb857b.description: Ladislas of Naples, Croat king and a claimant to the Hungarian throne as King Ladislav of Anjou, sells Dalmatia to the Venetians for 100,000 ducats. By 1420 Venice controlled all of Dalmatia except for Dubrovnik.

466c0d04-9a33-5dc9-98ba-2583d24d9114.description: Napoleon Bonaparte (1804–14) becomes King of Italy.

4724c447-dacf-5b17-a34b-ea34ad86b28b.description: Building of St Vitus Cathedral at Prague Castle commenced (master builder: Matthias of Arras, followed by Peter Parler). Foundation of Prague archbishopric.

4a5a39b4-d5cf-5a8c-8ac4-2faf4af371c3.description: Wenceslas IV inherits Czech crown. Completion of the oldest Czech translation of the Bible. Klaret’s (Claretus) attempt to create Czech scholarly terminology. Discord among the king, his brothers and the aristocracy.

4ced54f9-baa4-5555-8e2a-7b361cf7396d.description: Birth of Albrecht von Wallenstein (1583–1634), Duke of Friedland, who became the foremost general of emperor Ferdinand II (1619–37) of the Habsburg Dynasty in the Thirty Years’ War.

4d95a62e-4e83-5ce4-bfae-13c434a83563.description: King Charlemagne (768–814) is crowned as emperor in Rome by Pope Leo III (795–816).

4f289ff9-49ca-538c-8979-16d6ce06b7c9.description: March on Rome: the event confirms the rise to power of Benito Mussolini’s National Fascist Party and the beginning of the Fascist regime (1922–43).

5174eedb-90ec-5bd3-803f-0bb9ae7c7f28.description: Start of the islamicisation of al-Andalus. First incursions in al-Gharb.

51d0cc2b-2f6e-5aa9-bc2e-28a4f56d882a.description: Birth of Nikolaus von Kues (1401–64). His De docta ignorantia is notable for his mystical beliefs. He suggested the earth was a nearly spherical shape that revolved around the Sun.

533e7f21-74d3-595e-9cd5-de184ef0b43d.description: On the death of King András III the Árpád house dies out in the male line. Fights for the Hungarian throne ensue. The coronation of Károly I Róbert of Anjou (Caroberto), descended from the Árpád female line.

53554368-e4ff-5893-9708-a8ca4e8ac972.description: The start of the Thirty Years’ War (1618–48) between Protestants and Catholics; the war has disastruous results, including death, poverty and serious economic stagnation.

550074ba-6a67-5aa2-805c-4455e641f7a7.description: Foundation of Budapest with the unification of Buda, Pest and Óbuda. Plans by architect Miklós Ybl for the opera house in Budapest. Celebration of the 50th annniversary of Liszt’s musical career.

550f9918-555f-5156-bcf7-adff580601cf.description: Death of John II and ascension of Manuel I.

55f1c813-6382-52ac-b7ce-d6a466f841e4.description: The Muslim fleet is defeated by the Pisans at Palermo.

56e3c86a-efe5-5d89-a5fc-8d97d945087e.description: Estates defeated at Battle of White Mountain resulting in mass punishment and persecution. Uprising of the Wallachians (Carpathian pastoral culture). Charles University made over to the Jesuits.

5725b783-08b2-5794-be15-ecbae93c4959.description: First French invasion. The Portuguese court takes refuge in Brazil.

596bb1ac-89c8-5821-8a4f-b051a40c3713.description: Charlemagne (800–14) becomes the Emperor of Rome and the Holy Roman Empire is born.

5a23672f-8ed4-59a6-969b-b1748f2c2eb0.description: Karlóca Peace Treaty between the Holy Alliance and the Turks. The Sultan promises not to support Hungarian anti-Habsburg revolts (such as that of Imre Thököly who had earlier lost his freedom fight).

5a2d6c02-2916-54c4-9a78-da5d284005a2.description: Highlights of the Czech radical baroque: construction of Church of St. Nicholas, Prague, began (architect K. Dienzenhofer). Charles Bridge embellished with statues by M. B. Braun and F. Brokof.

5a8fce95-4d55-5e56-b3af-00e338bdfc22.description: Olomouc Agreement: Matthias Corvinus rules Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia, Vladislav Jagellon rules Bohemia. After Matthias’s death (1490) Vladislav appointed King of Hungary.

5b25240c-33ca-5eec-8b70-d7e280872199.description: Croatia forms a state union with Austria. By a decision of the Croatian Assembly, the dynasty of Habsburg comes to the Croatian throne.

5b6486bb-cd9c-5306-8dd6-153656ec18e6.description: Peace with Spain, which recognises Portuguese independence.

5b9d48a4-ebc4-5f5a-aa61-eb19b277201d.description: Frederick Barbarossa (1123–90) arrives in Italy to side with the Pope against the Commune of Rome and the Normans. In the same year, Barbarossa is crowned King of Italy in Pavia.

5ba39f99-c9e6-5c61-803e-2945fa3237a9.description: Charles IV appointed Margrave of Moravia.

5c4b0c8c-e56a-5e1f-bc18-53b6e91bac51.description: Charles IV is the first Czech sovereign to be crowned Holy Roman Emperor. In 1356 he issued the Golden Bull confirming the autonomous Czech state and making the Czech king foremost among the electors.

5c8b0092-ea67-5876-99cc-c64c2f57215f.description: Birth of Saint Fructuosus of Braga.

5ce9c4ba-9614-50ff-be1b-1f57c992b5e8.description: Charles IV elected Roman king. The period of his rule embraced the greatest flourishing of the Czech lands. Origination of the Czech crown jewels. Cult of St Wenceslas disseminated.

5d68f24f-1476-5605-8566-46a1180bca7f.description: Beginning of the Western Schism, which will divide the Christian Church and see two different popes on the papal seat.

5dffebe3-f733-570b-a1cb-e69c69f7e91a.description:
According to some, the Croatian kingdom was established and Duke Tomislav became its first king.  
The first Church Synod is held in Split.

5f96410c-5426-5d04-a979-cf55fa6822be.description: Hungarian King Ladislaus Pohrobek takes the Czech throne. Order to evict Jews from royal towns. George of Poděbrady elected Czech king (1485). Attempt to create union of European rulers aiming to avert Turkish expansion, restrict Catholic church hegemony and secure peace.

5fdefba5-ee86-5206-b36d-bc70dd7d5ffc.description: Sack of Rome: the imperial forces of Charles V (1520–56) made up of mercenaries (lanzichenecchi) sack Rome. This event is considered to mark the end of the Renaissance.

601c04ff-3177-5686-8eab-7344969f5a7b.description: Hus burned at the stake at the assembly of the Council of Constance. Struggles between Catholics and Utraquists (“heretics”). Crusades, plundering of monasteries and churches, iconoclasm.

605466fd-8f46-5ea9-be1c-420fea02de1b.description: Restoration of independence under John IV and the start of the Bragança Dynasty.

606a9fb4-1bd0-5070-b14c-8900f8bf5f93.description:
Governor Camilio Gonzaga establishes the city of Split. He proposed to the Venetian Senate to build a bulwark to defend the town.  
The Paulist School of philosophy was established.

609af117-9971-5451-9a1f-4295cf6f19a1.description: Revolt of the Sicilian Vespers against Sicily’s French Angevin rulers. Aragon emerges victorious in Sicily, which is separated politically from Southern Italy.

6127f939-9a01-5138-9480-d31c41ee1486.description: Great victories over Turks in north Croatia. The commanders of the victorious army were Banus Nikola Erdödy, General Leslie and Johann Joseph Herberstein.

61ac4c79-4d5d-57a9-b068-1f6d8d4d96ce.description: Under Duke Henry of Saxony the term ‘Kingdom of the Germans’ (Regnum teutonicum) is used for the first time.

61e06a93-5499-505f-92d5-1168822ce9f8.description: Bramante begins construction of the new Basilica of Saint Peter.

62562311-e5ba-55ea-b3e2-433a47297d68.description: The Ninth Symphony of the composer Ludwig van Beethoven (1770–1827) is seen as the peak of Viennese classical music.

62abb4f0-9df2-5b53-85f4-34d97a4dbc6d.description: The first reform-diet in Pozsony (Pressburg, today: Bratislava, Slovakia) where Count István Széchenyi donates one year’s income from his estates to establish the Hungarian Academy of Sciences.

638f6e99-278f-5f7f-895c-44d5889afae6.description: The recapture of Buda by the allied armies of the Holy Alliance led by Karl von Lothringen (Charles of Lorraine). The last Pasha of Buda dies in the struggle.

63e8e1ab-e526-50a6-ad12-4df446132691.description: The war between Germany and France results in a German victory and a proclamation of a German Empire (1871–1918) in Versailles with Wilhelm I of the Hohenzollern Dynasty as German Emperor.

643385d8-3b35-5cfe-8d8b-e840dd72e75b.description: Publication of *Ratio Educationis*, Maria Theresia’s school reform. The Nagyszombat University (Tyrnau; today: Trnava, Slovakia), founded by Bishop Péter Pázmány in 1635, moves to Buda.

64e12b06-ca69-5f0b-b431-c9da2312f6d9.description: The arrival of the Aghlabids triggers the Arab conquest of Sicily.

6614551e-35c4-5e1d-9b22-56146c5e1218.description: Konradin, son of King Konrad IV of the Hohenstaufen Dynasty, is beheaded. This ends the German emperorship in Italy.

6658849f-5a95-51e2-96e3-8d555f7f9a37.description: The first printed work issued in the Czech lands: Statutes for the Prague Diocese (Pilsen printing works).

66819408-ffeb-5693-9439-f4a007a5b805.description: Garibaldi leads the Expedition of the Thousand, and the second war of independence spreads to the South. Thanks to Garibaldi, the Kingdom of Sardinia annexes the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.

683badad-c3b8-59a7-a34b-476298abb624.description: Christopher Columbus discovers America. Lorenzo de’Medici dies.

6851eb46-610e-52f5-a3b5-0231697af1c3.description: Election of Gábor Bethlen (Protestant Transylvanian prince) as King of Hungary. He leads a freedom fight against the Habsburgs and brings cultural and economic prosperity to Transylvania.

68e74c54-2e2f-5d68-8283-84bb95aa155e.description: Treaty of Tordesillas between the Catholic Kings and John II, dividing the world into two spheres of influence: the Portuguese part and the Spanish part.

6aa37818-d1c4-5c89-ba5a-b70666930ea3.description: Croatian king Stjepan I (1030–58) focused on rebuilding Croatia’s military strength and in 1032 he sent his naval fleet to assist Byzantium in its war against the Arabs.

6aae110b-44cf-5bd2-80fc-b7ea4b8b6569.description: The Congress of Vienna restores the pre-Napoleonic fragmentation of Italian lands, and the hegemony of the Austrian Empire over the peninsula is sanctioned.

6ecac650-fc84-572a-accc-86ffb5d01fef.description: Start of the Muladi revolts against their Umayyad rulers in the west of the peninsular.

6f2bd13d-6676-566d-a87a-a637c49389f2.description: Two peace treaties: Vienna ends Hungary’s fight against the Habsburgs led by István Bocskai, Transylvanian prince; Zsitvatorok (part of Dunaradvány, today: Žitava, Slovakia) ends the fight with the Turks. Bocskai dies.

6f83ba51-b28e-53db-8324-60c8a90da048.description: First edition of The Lusiads by Luís de Camões.

700f81d2-6d59-587d-944c-8a9dce333cc5.description: The assasination of Austria’s crown prince leads to the beginning of the First World War in which Germany fights on the sides of the Central Powers against the Allied Powers.

71501d22-d2d0-5d4f-869c-2fa172e66945.description: Jesuits build the Church of St Catherine in Zagreb, from its architecture and inventory one of the most outstanding Jesuit churches in Croatia.

71e62ebe-3caa-5398-b35a-5694d1ba3aaf.description: Appearance of the first taifa kingdoms in al-Andalus.

72e16cd9-e290-5ea1-9890-0f13dfd05aa2.description: The Guelphs and Ghibellines, supporters of the Papacy and the Emperor respectively, clash in Florence.

731ef223-95e2-56a7-ac6d-314d9575401c.description: The poet, historian and philosopher Friedrich Schiller (1759–1805) finishes his drama Die Räuber, a great success in the Sturm und Drang Period.

7363747e-8773-5a7d-ba94-ddc2413fa105.description: The beatification of St. John of Nepomuk, drowned in the Vltava (Prague) in 1393. The most popular saint in the Czech lands, Lower Austria and southern Germany.

7387c09e-d3d0-501e-870f-cbe88a77b2db.description: Battle of Aljubarrota. Beginning of the Avis Dynasty with John I.

73f8a350-5aeb-5dd4-ae79-e1cb83ffbcf6.description: King of Portugal attacks the Algarve region.

745e109f-95e9-5474-9425-ff3eb3d699c7.description: The Danube’s great flood destroys a huge part of Pest. Contract signed to build the first permanent bridge (today: Széchenyi Lánchíd) between Buda and Pest initiated by Count István Széchenyi.

74d90b1b-5c76-5b75-b8dd-7b75a30e401f.description: Restored administration. The highest Czech administrative institutions transferred to Vienna. German made equal with Czech, Catholicism became the only religion. Extensive confiscations and emigrations.

75d6806c-b93f-5b40-9613-21b5a8edba1b.description: Unsuccesful peasant revolt led by György Dózsa. The presentation to the Hungarian Parliament of the *Tripartitum*, a collection of Hungarian unwritten laws compiled by jurist István Werbőczy (published Vienna, 1518).

764a56af-53f8-5a84-8c21-89a2c8dea758.description: King Matyas II approves the new Statute of the Zagreb Gradec.

7674de62-34de-568f-b510-86953b20a792.description: Josef II dies in February shortly after withdrawning all of his reforms concerning Hungary except for three. The Holy Crown of Hungary is again in Buda. Farkas (Wolfgang) Kempelen builds a speech-imitating machine.

7709d542-2f1e-51e1-b0dc-a06ab16d0054.description: The French occupy the lands of the Papal States and proclaim the Roman Republic.

78b031be-d165-527f-9cf9-37194a51d892.description: In the Treaty of Mersen the Frankish Empire is divided into three separate parts. The empire of King Ludwig II (843–76) of the Carolingian Dynasty is enlargened.

79f9a637-c261-59da-b67c-3756d93a7564.description: Discovery of the Cabo Verde archipelago.

7a2162f6-ae55-5c5e-852a-5daf6bccda7d.description: Creation of the United Kingdom of Portugal and Brazil.

7a9c7dc4-f410-5dd2-a7c7-3f2fdce68539.description: Emperor Wilhelm II (1888–1918) sacks Chancellor Otto von Bismark. The era is called ‘Wilhelminische Ära’ and eventually leads to the First World War.

7b281bdd-cc35-5add-a90e-751567cf4a99.description: Benito Mussolini Fasci Italiani di Combattimento (Italian Combat Groups) in Milan.

7ce987ab-fb3e-51a9-9a3d-1597fd2062e1.description: Galileo is tried by the Inquisition for his scientific theories.

7de8e5e8-5268-5abe-869d-19d2836112ed.description: Methuen Treaty between Portugal and the United Kingdom.

7ed30f2e-cf9a-53cb-8092-5da08c634936.description: French troops besiege Germany. Fighting only ends with the Treaty of the Congress of Vienna (1815). This ultimately results in a reformed Germany.

822a3247-fb33-5414-8db1-3370ec029661.description: *Pacta conventa* between Hungarian King Koloman and Croatia. Koloman Arpadović crowned as Croatian king in Biograd and the personal union established.

822ca493-3d5d-5c20-b52f-ec876c8a234f.description: Battle of Alcácer Quibir (also known as Battle of the Three Kings) during which King Sebastian dies.

828088ef-e842-5cef-917e-93df39c32af0.description: The Battle of Nikápoly: Sultan Bayazid I defeats the crusaders of King Sigismund of Luxemburg, sole ruler of Hungary after the death of his first wife, Queen Mary, daughter of Lajos (Louis) I in 1395.

8352c59f-ef4d-5a6a-aad9-aa35c8dfd5e1.description: Enlightenment leads to the creation, under the Grand Duke of Tuscany Pietro Leopoldo (1765–90), of a new penal code. The death penalty and torture are abolished for the first time in Europe.

83708617-033d-5862-8c7b-7053531e0053.description: Sulayman I the Great occupies Buda. Hungary torn into three parts: Turkish *vilajet* (province); Upper Hungary under Ferdinand I; the rest under Queen Isabella and János II (János Zsigmond), son of the Queen and János I.

84281e35-ee9e-57b7-9f43-93592b0bafaf.description: Beginning with the Battle of Tertry in 687 the Carolingian Dynasty rules over larger parts of the Germanic tribes.

870bb99e-6586-55f0-abab-48c565c7b410.description: Death of Meister Eckhart (1260–1328), a Dominican monk who was a theologian, philosopher and mystic. His writings on metaphysics and mysticism were of importance for the intellectual spirit of the late Middle Ages.

8797b214-12ac-5050-a37b-cd30f3ebe862.description: Coronation of (St) István who affirms his authority over the Hungarian leaders (e.g. in 1003 over Gyula in Transylvania) and establishes Hungary’s legal, administrative and ecclesiastical system.

87a1dfb6-5628-5377-81f2-578c46488414.description: The Battle of Mohács: the 75–80 000 Turkish soldiers defeat the Hungarian army of 25,000 men. King Lajos II dies. Both János I (Szapolyai) and Ferdinand I became Hungarian kings.

87ac0efc-fc67-5317-8b0c-a7133e71c414.description: The Portuguese Inquisition starts its work. Jesuits arrive in Portugal.

881eb6bf-2e0a-547d-95ed-4021999cc8f4.description: The oldest German code of law (Sachsenspiegel), written by Eike von Repgow (ca.1180–d. after 1233) in Latin and translated to German appears in final form. It becomes a standard for all future codes of law.

88e6bfe7-200a-58dc-960e-face7cfe9ab3.description: Entry of Miklós Horthy (governor of Hungary from 1920) to Budapest as head of the national army ends the 133 days’ rule of a communist regime (Tanácsköztársaság) led by Béla Kun.

89496679-1b62-5ad7-9bb3-5373f5485251.description: Beginning of the Seven Years’ War between Prussia, Austria, Russia and France about the territories of Saxonia and Silesia. Prussia becomes a European power.

8a015f91-7893-5c5c-84b5-2c277f7eb80c.description: Election of King Mátyás (Matthias) I Hunyadi (Corvinus) son of János Hunyadi. He made Hungary one of the greatest economical and military powers of Europe and defended Europe from the Turks.

8a9fc0fd-9822-51fc-a93e-13c523507294.description: The philosopher Immanuel Kant (1724–1804) publishes his book Kritik der praktischen Vernunft. He is considered a major philosopher of the Age of Enlightenment.

8b2783fc-861b-5ba3-baed-b7735c848827.description: Liberal victory in the civil war. Establishment of a constitutional monarchy.

8b6c7d09-3fa1-501e-a1c1-48b920954bc1.description:
Arrival of Jesuits in Zagreb. In 1607 they established the Classical Gymnasium, the first gymnasium (high school) that still exists today.  
Arrival of the first pharmacist J. Gasparini in Zagreb.

8d349448-3b35-57c6-b21c-6ef4bb86d48b.description: Count Ferenc Széchenyi donates his library and collections to the Hungarian nation. This is the nucleus of the National Museum of Hungary and of the National Széchenyi Library.

8e1f0cdb-9c8b-5a24-b1e8-a1ac0636af79.description: The policy of Wilhelm II toward the Near East results in his travels to the Ottoman empire (Istanbul, Jerusalem and Damascus).

8ef35caf-8ebb-56b9-b17b-f1c9254f54d2.description: Prussian–Austrian War. Establishment of workers’ associations. J. G. Mendel pioneers genetics. The foundation stone of the National Theatre, Prague laid (1868).

8f5544f4-323e-5497-9308-6e3815533e21.description: Decree of Kutná Hora adjusts the university voting rights between the Czechs and other nationalities. Jan Hus appointed university chancellor. Origins of the Hussite reformation movement, critical of church rule.

8fd4e3ba-c0ee-5264-9d50-aa3f6e67b9fa.description: The Battle of Varna: Sultan Murad II defeats the Hungarian army. King Ulaslo I dies but commander-in-chief János Hunyadi survives. Stripes and a double cross first appear together in Hungary’s coat of arms.

913c42fb-7154-55c4-977f-0ee1a1a19912.description:
In Varaždin the first Jewish commune is established.  
Joseph II announces his ‘Patent on the abolishment of slavery’ for the territories of Hungary and Croatia.  
The first Real Gymnasium is opened in Senj.

924ee5a3-044f-5833-9bfe-d7997e1b245b.description: The first Czech periodical newspaper (Prague). Moravian aristocracy in service of the empire. Viennese artists in Moravia. Development of pilgrimages; church celebrations.

93616fec-6e93-5c91-b200-a316a84855fc.description: Venice conquers Karlobag attacking Novi Vinodolski, the city of the Frankopans. This marks the beginning of the Austro-Venetian war, at this stage known as the Uskok war.

946ff306-90df-5596-b20b-d3b3eec99037.description: The ‘Fundamental law’ for military territory (the so-called ‘Vojna krajina’ of the Varaždin and Karlovac military district) in Croatia is established.

948f192d-9418-5767-bd74-07be3006527d.description: The Hungarian Jacobin Conspiracy’s members are executed or imprisoned. Archduke Josef becomes the new Hungarian Palatine. Pál Kitaibel invents a vacuum-filtering process.

95007cb7-2411-5908-9912-f4ac0318ec59.description: Olomouc bishopric promoted to archbishopric. Foundation of a bishopric in Brno. Abolition of serfdom. Riots of the Evangelicals in Wallachia.

9542a3ac-2190-5bee-b91e-51b826bf822f.description: The coronation of the last Hungarian royal couple, Charles IV and Zita. Romania declares war on Hungary and enters Transylvania. The Allies reject the peace note of the Central Powers.

98b2fb1f-f544-5da6-aa8c-97a3ec4a89bb.description: Vienna was surrounded by Turkish armies and Moravia was plundered before the Turks were forced back to the Balkans. The last Turkish war in Europe.

98d562cc-ceb6-54f8-aada-b85d5831c843.description: Muslim attack on Santarém, resulting in the death of Abu Ya‘qub Yusuf.

994f5373-9632-55b5-b291-1371d4b08d52.description: Umberto I (1878–1900) is assassinated by the anarchist Gaetano Bresci. He is succeeded by his son Victor Emanuel III (1900–46).

9a5d79f2-32bb-5fc4-b016-56a320be5388.description: The Golden Bull becomes the first constitution of the empire by which the German emperor is chosen by seven electors.

9aae350e-b26b-5b6c-a383-e96764bbc035.description: Zagreb and a major part of Croatia are stricken by plague of epidemic proportions.

9b4a021c-190f-579c-9bd7-3e9c7f6c2474.description: Around 30,000 Croatian soldiers, mainly cavalry, participate in the Thirty Years’ War. Croatian troops fight against Miklós Bethlen (1642–1716) in Bohemia and Hungary.

9d131feb-6757-5105-b9fb-13823b6eb9ce.description: The German polymath Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (1749–1832) is born. He became one of the leading figures of German literature during the period of classicism.

9e8721ac-e6ea-582d-a638-8daf754fd621.description: The reign of the Lombards comes to an end. Charles King of the Franks takes Pavia and establishes Frankish rule in Northern Italy. The Duchy of Benevento and Venice remain independent.

9e89f221-9ca5-59f1-8606-aa04b2f4f365.description: The Hungarian Diet accepts the Habsburgs’ female succession. Introduction of a Newcomen-type steam machine, the first in continental Europe, in Újbánya (Königsberg; today: Nová Baňa, Slovakia).

9f883ec3-a505-5d70-a96d-9ab380a7afac.description: Prague described in narration of Jewish-Arabian merchant Ibn Jákúb. Establishment of first (Benedictine) monasteries and Prague bishopric (974). Foundation of the Czech state under the Przemyslid dynasty.

a08eda40-bca2-5719-8b04-cc49f40936ac.description: On the initiative of the Council of Trent the Bishop of Zagreb, Juraj Drašković, establishes the Zagreb Seminary (Seminarium Clericorum) to promote theology.

a132dd55-8a57-52bb-8ffa-680053644859.description: The Council of the Lateran reorganises the Church. The Pope makes Robert Guiscard (1059–85) Duke of Puglia and Calabria. It is the first acknowledgement of Norman domination of Southern Italy.

a268be2a-e4af-530b-b61e-1295b532e932.description: King Konrad I (911–18) of the Conradine Dynasty becomes king.

a2a7510f-cadb-574a-b4ec-96cb5f860496.description: Sultan Sulayman I besieges Szigetvár defended by Count Miklós Zrínyi who getting no help and with heavy odds against him dies with his soldiers in a sortie. The Sultan had died two days earlier.

a308451b-8b67-52d5-b38b-135d2e6c485c.description: Napoleon incorporates Dalmatia, Dubrovnik and western Croatia as the French Illyrian Provinces. France stimulated agriculture and commerce in the provinces and fought piracy.

a311f432-76a7-5ee2-b78e-8d7d22ac2d17.description: Charles IV’s major projects: revival of Slavonic liturgy (1347); foundation of New Town (1348), making Prague the largest European city; establishment of Prague University, the first in Central Europe; provincial statutes in Brno and Olomouc.

a399bb09-24f2-5067-8434-aa65591c8291.description: Master Simon Kézai, a cleric of King László (Kun) IV, starts to compile the Gesta Hungarorum, a chronicle of Hungary (completed in 1285) that contains the theory of the Hun-Hungarian identity.

a39c69e0-1b68-56a4-a6fb-417fef818bc9.description: Italy enters World War I (1914–18) on the side of France, England and Russia.

a5cd38e3-f358-5794-b62f-e0b0898c4c91.description: Carolina Resolutio: Emperor Karl (Charles) VI (Karl III as king of Hungary) regulates Protestant affairs. England accepts the Pragmatic Sanction in return for economic advantages.

a5f38714-9ce5-579f-af5d-54483e90d885.description: The Commune of Rome is born, an expression of the nascent communal civility that will have a profound effect on Italian cultural identity.

a6bb8290-9387-5a36-b6cc-558c2389e269.description: Michelangelo Buonarroti starts work on David, a masterpiece of the Renaissance. The work, conceived as a symbol of the Florentine Republic, is completed in 1504.

a6e47bae-a6d8-592c-a3e6-3c7acfb9058b.description: As a result of the revolution in November 1918 Germany becomes a republic. Emperor Wilhelm II abdicates.

a72610e0-a8ae-564b-8415-d746e501c248.description: The papal residence moved back to Rome from Avignon during the pontificate of Gregory XI (1370–8).

a80ebf70-efcb-5413-adc1-03bbde6f3152.description: Wenceslas II crowned King of Bohemia. Minting of Prague kreuzers, the most sought-after European silver currency. Wenceslas crowned King of Poland 1300, of Hungary 1301. The murder of Wenceslas III (1306) ended male line of Przemyslid dynasty.

a8ee617c-104e-5a7c-aef4-ba101ed51d76.description: The Nibelungenlied is written down. During the Age of Chivalry numerous texts, ballads and songs were written by Minnesänger singers such as medieval lyricist Walter von der Vogelweide (c.1170–c.1230).

a916becc-4482-5837-8a8d-43b179b21088.description: Charlemagne (r. 768–814) inherits the Frankish crown and becomes king of a large part of Europe and the founder of a Roman, Christian and Germanic empire.

a92c157c-3c17-59df-8252-8bb9548ef497.description: Spread of Christianity, arrival of missionaries Constantine (Cyril) and Methodius; establishment of Old Slavonic language, Glagolitic script. Archbishopric established. Conflicts with Frankish empire, invasions of Hungarian tribes. The foundation of Prague Castle.

a96ee6d7-e854-5751-9dae-7d7254e74791.description: Pope Urban V affirms the Paulite order, founded by Hungarians c. 1250. King Lajos (Louis) I founds Pécs University and enriches Aachen Cathedral’s Hungarian Chapel with great artworks.

a97b046a-dda3-5a7b-96dc-abad080cb561.description: Frederick of Aragon (1302–37) is proclaimed King of Sicily.

ab4ce6ac-5c1a-5d07-b5a9-9b2e5ef6d50d.description: Battle of Lipany, defeat of the Hussites. Sigismund of Luxemburg crowned Czech king (1436). The Basle “Compacts” acknowledging the communion of bread and wine.

ab694c91-8c7f-5bbe-9396-14f4a359f36f.description: Start of the Avignon Papacy: under the direct influence of the King of France, the popes set up the papal residence in Avignon.

ab7a01fa-6720-5502-adea-c007f6276c2e.description: The peace of Zadar seals the defeat of the Venetian Republic by Louis of Anjou, King of Hungary–Croatia, and marks the reunification of Dalmatia with the Croatian crown within a common kingdom.

abdf391f-644b-5f0d-8a81-b054cf32f4c6.description: Compromise with the House of Habsburg (activated by Ferenc Deák on the Hungarian side). Emperor Franz Joseph I crowned King of Hungary in Buda. Birth of the Austro-Hungarian Monarchy.

ac5cc8e1-67e0-5974-a73f-969d58d801c2.description: Battle of Mohacs. Ludwig Jagellon defeated by the Turks, the dynasty died out. According to a contract from 1515, the Czech throne passes to the Habsburg dynasty. Anti-Habsburg movement of the Czech Estates.

ad7b4406-5458-5692-bd4b-012025a822cf.description: Census: 3 million people in the Czech lands. Introduction of astandardised system of measures and weights. P. Diviš constructed the first lightning conductor. V. A. Kounic-Rietberg became court and state chancellor.

ad963d8a-95f6-55f2-b190-825142f300fe.description: Completion of Karlštejn Castle: Emperor’s residence housing the Czech and imperial crown jewels, the archive and relics of saints. The construction of the Stone (now Charles) Bridge, Prague.

ae70c88a-d91f-5c16-8cab-452584c501b2.description: Szatmár Peace Treaty ends the unsuccessful freedom fight of Prince Ferenc Rákóczi II. Publication of *Harmonia Coelestis* composed by Prince Pál Esterházy, Palatine of Hungary.

afbb3468-d841-584b-8608-021a505874de.description: Birth of the painter, wood carver and engraver Albrecht Dürer (1471–1528). During this period Renaissance art flourished in Germany and Dürer travelled to Italy twice.

afcdd58b-7839-5a59-ac2f-64d9629edb2b.description: In the church of Our Lady of Pirates in Komiža on the island of Vis Stjepan Killarevich from Krakow builds one of three preserved 17th-century organs in Croatia.

b0494ea6-578b-5895-b717-63d9e50b574c.description: Reforms under Emperor Joseph II: tolerance patent permitting non-Catholicism (Catholicism remains the official religion). Abolition of serfdom. Closure of monasteries not dedicated to publicly beneficial work.

b06b82d6-f264-5dd3-825a-3dee0d5bdf7e.description: Henry IV is forced to abdicate and is followed by King Henry V (1106–25) of the Salian Dynasty.

b154123d-1877-5dba-bf9a-be805ad9136d.description: Edict of the Byzantine Emperor Leon III by which he excluded western Balkan lands, the entire Illyrics, from the authority of the Roman Pope and submitted them to the Byzantine patriarch.

b311cbdc-2e6e-58a2-902c-ba5ac57b1df1.description: On 9 July Nikola Tesla is born in Croatia.

b3b47577-dfd4-5d5f-a79a-10dea5dd3198.description: Giordano Bruno, philosopher and theologian, is burned at the stake in Rome, condemned by the Church for heresy. His death marks one of the darkest and tragic moments of the Counter-Reformation.

b451acf8-4cf6-5310-951c-adbf320d8252.description: Franz II (1768–1835), Austrian Emperor, lays down the German crown and thus dissolves the Holy Roman Empire of the German Nation.

b5b257ce-33b8-5e51-be99-467ed2709a52.description: Manfred, son of Frederick II, becomes King of Sicily (1258–66).

b630bcdb-b5e1-5ccc-92ef-ced5dcc803c2.description: After the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife Emperor Franz Joseph I leads the Austro-Hungarian monarchy into World War I on the sides of the Central Powers. Beginning of Hungarian aircraft industry.

b6b6442f-b24b-51f6-bfa5-a22990d3c290.description: Adherents of Martin Luther, the German religious reformer, appear in Prague. Outbreak of conflicts among Catholics, Utraquists and Lutherans. Anabaptists in Moravia.

b7382ca1-131e-50df-9131-54e3bea10770.description: ‘Abd al-Rahman III lays siege to Beja and Faro. Establishment of the Caliphate of Córdoba.

b796f1ba-424c-5f89-be87-930d89114f5d.description: Lorenzo de’Medici the Magnificent (1469–92) rules Florence. Under his control, Florence becomes the driving force behind Italian art.

b9324a46-5740-5257-902f-e4f5838a4a61.description: Charlemagne dies in Aachen (Aix-la-Chapelle) on 28 January 814 and is buried in the palatine chapel of Aachen.

bb7e934e-c0ba-5b13-b971-e251144d52e6.description: On 25–28 January Emperor Henry IV (1056–1106) of the Salian Dynasty is forced on a walk of penitence to Canossa to beg forgiveness of Pope Gregor VII and to accept him as arbitrator. The Way (or Walk) to Canossa refers to the walk itself and the events surrounding his journey.

bc3b3323-7fae-5c2d-ac31-334e9e02ad95.description: King Otto II (r. 973–83) marries the Byzantine princess Theophanu and Byzantine influence enters German art and culture.

bd1b6b63-774d-5ba8-9c15-dc930b92a918.description: Law separating the Church and the State.

bd343c99-27e3-5c4b-bb3b-f2df20dc01e7.description: Maria Theresa ascends throne (d. 1780). Invasion of the Prussian army leads to inheritance wars over the Czech crown. Unifying style known as ’Pragmatic Sanction in art’.

bd79b189-901c-53b8-8c01-13ed41e37029.description: The reign of Henry II (1002–24) sees the establishment of a feudal system, particularly in Northern Italy, which will leave a lasting mark on Italy’s social and economic make-up.

bd89acfb-d8f6-568b-92ae-49e1bb2ac269.description: Victory of Charles Martel (688–741) of the Carolingian Dynasty at the battle of Tours and Poitiers (southern France) over Arab insurgents leads to their retreat to the southern valley of the Rhone.

bf67fc00-6bd0-5727-ac0f-20e9d1498c7f.description: In Torgau in Saxonia the first German opera ‘Dafne’ composed by Heinrich Schütz (1595–1672) is first performed.

c21f0c27-a07a-5849-8995-05cbd4864748.description: The first Normans arrive in Southern Italy.

c3b71cc6-5c01-565c-80e1-f38e0b6388ec.description: During the rule of the Merovingian Dynasty (c. 500–751) Germanic tribes become subjects of the Merovingian Dynasty.

c4f654dc-230d-51a2-83d8-f1739a177801.description: Dante Alighieri begins his masterpiece of universal literature, the Divine Comedy, completed in 1313.

c5868ee4-677f-5acb-8d91-5b2138dd0739.description: Friedrich III, Elector of Brandenburg, is crowned as Friedrich I, King of Prussia. Prussia is on its way to becoming a European power.

c5f42106-3d50-5589-96f8-126417ad5acc.description: According to the double conquest theory of Gyula László the origin of the first archaeological finds in the Carpathian basin indicate the presence of the first wave of the Hungarian tribes.

c633dc65-ddff-50d9-a12e-0d5b24a1a309.description: The Lombards officially convert to Catholicism, a process that began with the work of Gregory the Great.

c63b9f28-eddf-5cd4-b4ee-786569fedc4b.description: Birth of Johann Sebastian Bach (1685–1750), who is seen as one of the foremost composers of concertos, cantatas and oratorios in the Western tonal tradition.

c6c268bb-310b-5ebc-8344-4b4a41af2e0b.description: The land of Thuringia is conquered by rulers of the Merovingian Dynasty with the help of the Saxons.

c6e5022f-f08c-5dd9-9dcb-09026fd7a1cf.description: Union of the German Reich with the Kingdom of Burgundy under King Konrad II (1024–39) of the Salian Dynasty.

c7682417-b27b-5a30-bbb0-a416f4c56167.description: Largest uprising of the serfs. Patents of King Leopold I include: corvée patent, legalisation of the Evangelical church (1691). The first textile manufactories.

c7ea97cc-341a-5208-a19f-5d77291da059.description: Roger I of Hautville (1072–1101) begins the conquest of Sicily against the Arabs, which is completed in 1091.

c8615122-0767-51d3-923d-870ef6f7ac28.description: The siege of Siget. Nikola Šubić Zrinski holds out against the army of the Sultan Sulayman I and falls during the last attack.

c96f8040-42eb-5743-9634-cc66fa039b22.description: Emperor Rudolph II transfers his court to Prague, which became a major European centre of politics, science and arts (de Brahe, Kepler). The first public autopsy (Ján Jesenský, 1600).

c9a68ec1-633f-5c5b-b031-b4f4ac1c9226.description: John of Luxemburg marries Elizabeth Przemyslid. First Czech-langauge publication *Dalimil Chronicle* (1314); the first guild code in the Czech lands published (1318).

ca0bad88-b336-5fa2-b5a5-b7e3a327b654.description: Croats establish the principalities of Primorska Hrvatska on the Adriatic Coast and Posavska Hrvatska in north Croatia.

ccf46a7e-06ed-53cb-ac3b-69a8eab5d353.description: Death of Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (1646–1716), last universal genius in Germany and founder of the Prussian Academy of Science, who made major contributions in philosophy and mathemathics.

cd3f2129-dd10-57cb-ac55-26226f6d2151.description: The Corpus Iuris Civilis is compiled under Justinian, collecting and organising Roman law. The work remains influential for centuries, becoming the cornerstone of legal studies.

cfaa47bd-78ef-5bf4-afa3-da894161b359.description: The first seigniories are formed, in Milan under Filippo della Torre, in Ferrara with Obizzo d’Este and in Mantova with the Gonzaga family.

d115668a-2742-5316-a253-9681b4ce5136.description: J. Janský publishes his discovery of four blood groups. Introduction of the right to vote. Workers’ strikes. The first permanent cinema.

d18a39fe-f15a-5b08-aed5-7509c8988e7e.description: Croats settle in the area between the Adriatic Sea and the Sava and Drava rivers.

d1f96c1e-0b95-5443-a8a4-f889d0839007.description: The composer Richard Wagner (1813–83) writes his opera Tristan and Isolde. This is a new form of musical theatre and musical language which he calls music drama.

d37e749f-84d3-5b8d-94f4-08d149e70a3a.description: End of the Christian conquest of the west of the peninsula.

d4608d7d-9ec1-5c7a-a8c7-e445a663301c.description: The March Revolution tried to introduce a democratic constitution. Marx (1818–83) and Engels (1820–95) publish Das Kommunistische Manifest analysing capitalist methods of production.

d4d0ecd5-1fe4-5fe3-9adc-574a05e4eae8.description: Galileo Galilei finishes his telescope and publishes Starry Messenger, prompting scientific reflection that plunges the Church’s thinking on the universe into crisis for the first time.

d5db1a23-db05-5440-93d4-1daac0613577.description: End of the monarchy (revolution of 5 October).

d62e451c-4725-5e18-9684-3e192db9a7f1.description: Lisbon earthquake. Reconstruction of the city begins under the auspices of the Prime Minister, the Marquis of Pombal.

d97a011f-47ca-5292-a77d-ef9057d698b7.description: Death of Paracelsus (1493–1541), physician, philosopher and writer of medical treatments, who was a defender of empirical medicine and rejected Gnostic traditions.

d98b47f0-d06e-539a-a09c-e32ae6b3f81f.description: Assembly of non-Catholic Estates. ’Prague Defenestration’ incident sparked a rising of the Czech Estates against the Habsburgs and the outbreak of the Thirty Years’ War. Czech Estates joined by Moravian and Austrian aristocracy and Frederick, Elector Palatine (Czech king 1619–20).

d9a8f554-2ebe-5f4e-9445-d97665d76a8d.description: The invention of the printing machine with movable metal types by Johannes Gutenberg (c. 1398–c. 1468) results in the first printing of the Gutenberg Bible (Biblia Sacra) in 1455.

dae4e9bb-b325-5f00-bd71-07256ef0c732.description: As a part of the freedom fight of Prince Ferenc Rákóczi II against the Habsburgs (began in 1703) the Parliament of Ónod declares the Habsburg dynasty deposed in Hungary.

dc191563-3d33-511a-9a93-5ce19fc1971e.description: Jesuits build their church in Varaždin dedicated to the Assumption of Virgin. The church is considered to follow the style of the Roman church Il Gesù.

ddc7fedb-bc65-592f-a5c5-fc5f833688ea.description: Displeased with the king’s rule noblemen force King András II to sign the Golden Bull that limits his power. In another order the king strengthens the privileges of the ecclesiastical order.

de5e9b65-2e7c-5457-8e54-a30dcb3830d7.description: Expounding his economic and social programme (including regulation of the lower Danube) Count István Széchenyi publishes *Hitel* (Credit) the first Hungarian socio-economic reform programme.

e11682f1-f9fb-54a0-853a-62fa703a01a8.description: End of the Thirty Years’ War. The Peace of Westphalia is signed in Münster and Osnabrück and results in a territorial agreement for Germany.

e16a040b-793f-51f7-9b57-85e3c3169ecd.description: Work starts on the palace-convent of Mafra, commissioned by John V (r. 1705–50).

e2b2b3e3-b1bb-5be9-8ef6-e84ce21118a4.description: Start of Portuguese expansion in Morocco with the conquest of Ceuta.

e2db2a61-6998-5313-b9de-02518b18d102.description: Battle of São Mamede. Afonso Henriques takes control of the Portucuese Counties.

e32c09c5-5af6-5efe-866c-9cc154000c7d.description: Fraternal Union. The origination of an independent church picking up the threads of Hussite ideology. War in Moravia. Matthias Corvinus against George of Poděbrady.

e3a7cd38-dcbf-5ed1-9516-27dcdd55dc71.description: Establishment of the Czech Academy of Science. K. V. Klíč invents photogravure. The first automobile with a combustion engine in the monarchy (1897); first Czech motorbike and cinema (1898). Widespread emigration to the USA due to the economic depression.

e4d90de4-9b5b-532b-a3b0-b00cb57ee573.description: Germany is proclaimed a Republic and on 11 August the Weimar Constitution comes into effect with Friedrich Ebert as its first president.

e6281845-dd0f-5aef-b735-c920d3402e81.description: V. M. Kramerius publishes the first Czech revival newspaper, the first mass reading material in the Czech language in 170 years.

e7604f15-59a4-586a-a398-8c61aee6632e.description: Beginning of the Reformation. Luther nails his 95 theses against the abuse of indulgences to a church door in Wittenberg. His translation of the Bible established the basis of the modern German language.

e8ab353d-bf8b-5d88-8814-da3ed5dbc56a.description: Vasco da Gama leaves for India.

e96448e3-55e1-557c-ac2e-50b08d4a2769.description: The Hungarian King Ladislas establishes the Zagreb Diocese.

ea2019a3-c616-5ed7-a95f-c8558cdbc1dc.description: Deposing of the House of Habsburg. Lajos Kossuth appointed as governor of Hungary. The freedom fight is lost; Hungarian general Görgey capitulates at Világos to the Habsburg’s Russian allies..

eac5ae58-b5c0-5eed-9437-0100eea3088f.description: Council of Burgos abolishes the Mozarabic rite in favour of the Roman rite.

eb053965-52cc-5b07-aa5c-fe769ba24ede.description: Bourgeois revolution demanding end of absolutism, equality of Czech with German, freedom of the press and religion. Abolition of serfdom and the corvée obligation. Slavic Assembly tries to found a Slavic association within the monarchy and turn it into a federal state.

eb63b5ef-7820-5fcb-afed-ebe8e69c77e0.description: Third war of independence: Italy succeeds in freeing the Veneto region from Austrian control.

ebc2c885-d678-5fee-93b2-3fa1e58d8736.description: On 29 October the Croatian Parliament proclaims Croatia’s administrative relations with Austria and Hungary void. In December the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes is formed.

ec709300-7a95-5a5c-8d72-2de7b3d8af5d.description: Millenium celebrations. Opening of the continent’s first underground railway in Budapest. Alfréd Hajós is the first Olympic swimming champion. István Bugarszky invents the endothermic galvanic cell.

ed290351-7430-5b84-96bf-347aefda19ea.description: Second taifas in al-Gharb. Afonso Henriques recognised as king at the Zamora Conference.

edef4829-1262-5a98-a017-88819bd38ea5.description: In pursuit of a South Slav cultural union bishop Josip Strossmayer founds the Yugoslav Academy of Arts and Sciences.

ee062ba7-04a0-5019-8753-904b6cb19dd3.description: The first industrial exhibition in Klementinum, Prague. Beginnings of the Czech linguistics. Origins of the nationalist movement. Establishment of the Academy of Fine Arts in Prague (1799).

ee4256e6-5666-5a31-a9e6-d6da6febd361.description: Trpimir I issues a charter in Latin in which he names himself the ‘Duke of Croats’ (*Dux Chroatorum iuvatus munere divino*) and his realm as the ‘Realm of the Croats’ (*Regnum Chroatorum*).

ee95c212-74d3-56f4-8956-1a9119c04e7d.description: Přemysl Otakar II killed at Battle of the Moravian Field. Under his rule, the Czech lands reached to the shores of the Adriatic. Bohemia governed by Otto of Brandenburg, Moravia by Rudolph of Habsburg.

eeab8447-dc55-5cd4-94d2-8fa8bb81b8cc.description: The Fourth Crusade, which will last until 1204, leaves from Venice.

efd013c7-e8f7-5483-bfb9-25828148f10a.description: Conquest and settlement: the Hungarian tribes spread through the Carpathian basin led by Árpád, the father of the first Hungarian royal dynasty, the Árpáds, whose first king was (St) István (1000–38).

eff9e44f-51db-540b-b707-4da6699f8470.description: Peace of Westphalia marks the end of the Thirty Years’ War. Habsburg rule in the Czech lands officially acknowledged. Moravia lost almost half of its population. Inflow of foreign aristocracy. Brno became the capital of Moravia.

f1ff7639-4033-5e0c-b6d7-902452a2c98a.description: Foundation of the first German university in Prague by Emperor Charles IV.

f3323f91-afc4-516c-b719-8197385d3176.description: The Croatian–Hungarian King Bela IV grants the Golden Bull to Gradec, as a token of appreciation for the citizens who provided him shelter during the Tatarian invasion.

f532aa76-8e98-50eb-9e60-7cf66e41c1e9.description: Prussia, Austria and Russia gain a decisive battle against Napoleon I (1769–1821) near Leipzig. This is seen as the peak of the German freedom movement.

f5a6313c-2d95-5d8c-9483-d6331ff97cc7.description: Second war of independence: Austria declares war on the Kingdom of Sardinia. The war is initially fought in Northern Italy.

f5b653d8-31d9-55a2-af56-435f06f95ce3.description: Establishment of the independent Czechoslovak state after the end of the First World War. President T. G. Masaryk elected (1920) (d. 1937). Origins of the theory of art and art history institutions.

f686e0b2-b2b1-5423-b2ff-17a5b5b84789.description: Saint Francis of Assisi writes his Rule, inspired by the principles of poverty, errant preaching and Christian charity. Frederick II (1211–50), already King of Sicily, is crowned emperor.

f68ed818-b5d6-55ac-b001-1234072ebb05.description: Having already founded the Zagreb bishopric, King (St) László I founds the St Egid Benedictine monastery in Somogyvár (his first burial site before Várad [today: Oradea, Romania]), inviting monks from Saint Gilles.

f861b4bd-9242-5d70-ab83-9f9e261987bb.description: Pope Boniface VIII (1295–1303), in conflict with the French for political reasons, is arrested by the French, but immediately released following a popular uprising.

f8a09aa4-3ccf-5642-83ad-1ef5c9735a4f.description: With the decisive help of the Hungarian-Kun army Habsburg Rudolf I defeats the Czech army in the Battle of Dürnkrut (Morvamező). The beginning of the rise of the Habsburgs.

f9b87cd5-bbf5-539f-bdab-00e35114424f.description: F. Křižík invents the self-acting regulator of the arc lamp, the first electrical lighting. His invention was received to great worldwide acclaim. The first telephone network introduced (1882).

fa285095-032b-5ac5-8381-860f5162aa6e.description: Disputes between Rudolph II and his brother Matthias. Moravian Estates led by Karel of Žerotín join the associations of Austrian and Hungarian Estates. Imperial charter issued by Rudolph II confirms religious freedom (1609); however, discord continues.

fb457b89-6c95-5ccb-8e45-60315b658bd6.description: The Porta Pia Breach: on 20 September, the Sardinian army liberates Rome, annexing the city and the Papal States to the Kingdom of Italy. The unification of Italy is complete

fbc054da-daf1-5c48-a1ba-31bd3a6cf491.description: Foundation of the abbey at Alcobaça.

fc9dbab5-5199-5614-84b4-4672ce1422f1.description: Pope Alexander III’s papal bull Manifestis Probatum recognises the king of Portugal.

fce8de86-ba5a-56ee-93fd-630f2cff89b7.description: Justinian (527–65) becomes the Emperor of Byzantium and sets about reconquering the West, succeeding in destroying the Gothic Kingdom in Italy.

fd498872-9dac-5625-a271-b744c7c1c509.description: Golden Bull of Sicily: Roman King Friedrich II defines the relationship between Czech kings and the Holy Roman Empire. The Czech king becomes one of seven electors privileged to elect the Roman king.

fdd5fcc0-8adf-50c7-80cd-e1ce3e734c0d.description: The beginning of the Baroque city of Vukovar, building of the city centre, Franciscan monastery, parish church and the Palace of the Counts Eltz.

feb88445-6eb8-5380-8476-ecef67f86338.description: Death of Miklós Zrínyi, great Hungarian commander in the Turkish wars. Turks defeated in the Battle of Szentgotthárd but the Habsburgs’ deplorable Peace of Vasvár causes Hungarian revolt.

fef02460-9e3a-55ad-8396-71d1ac16429d.description: Declaration of the Papal Bull of the Dissolution of the Jesuit Order. Prince Miklós Esterházy entertains Queen Maria Theresia (Theresa) in Eszterháza with splendid festivities, including Haydn’s music.
